lessons.title: V and M, the index fingers on the bottom row
lessons.tip: V is typed by the left index finger and M by the right: your index fingers go down one row, below F and J, then return to their bump. Keep your other fingers resting on the home row.

tuto.intro: You move down to the bottom row, the one just below your home row. We start with the index fingers: V for the left hand, M for the right.

rules.t: The index finger goes down, then back up
rules.d: Your left index finger goes down to V, just below F. Your right index finger goes down to M, just below J. After each keystroke, it returns to its bump.
To reach down, curl your finger instead of stretching your whole hand. Your wrist may drop very slightly, but stays relaxed.
With V and M you can write me, mum, milk, very, have and visit. And a sentence: we have a very warm home.

tuto.tip: Goal: reach down to V and M with your index fingers, then return to F and J without looking.

lessons.text: vm mv; mum has milk; we have a very warm home; they visit a valley; we have five; move over

lessons.title: C and comma, the middle fingers on the bottom row
lessons.tip: C is typed by the left middle finger and the comma by the right, below D and K. The comma sticks to the word before it, then a space follows.

tuto.intro: C and the comma are typed with the middle fingers, below D and K. The comma is your first punctuation mark: it makes sentences easier to read.

rules.d: Your left middle finger goes down to C, below D. Your right middle finger goes down to the comma, below K. The movement goes down, not sideways.

rules.t: The comma sticks to the word
rules.d: Type the word, then the comma straight away with no space before it, then a space after: cake, cheese, coffee. Tidy punctuation makes your texts easy to read.
Your index fingers stay on F and J while your middle fingers reach down: they are your guides for getting back without looking.

tuto.tip: Goal: reach down to C and the comma without losing the home row, with a relaxed wrist.

lessons.text: c, ,c; cake, cheese, coffee, rice; cold cloud; coat, scarf, sock, cat; the teacher, the class, the school

lessons.title: X and full stop, the ring fingers on the bottom row
lessons.tip: X is typed by the left ring finger and the full stop by the right, below S and L. The full stop ends the sentence: it sticks to the last word.

tuto.intro: X and the full stop are typed with the ring fingers, below S and L. X is fairly rare but useful. The full stop ends every one of your sentences.

rules.d: Your left ring finger goes down diagonally to X, below S. Your right ring finger goes down to the full stop, below L. Do it slowly to learn it.

rules.t: The full stop ends the sentence
rules.d: It sticks to the last word, then a space follows: the taxi is here. the fox is there. For now, we write without capital letters.

rules.t: Go gently with the ring fingers
rules.d: These fingers are less agile than your index and middle fingers. A slow, accurate movement is better than a fast, wrong one.

tuto.tip: Goal: place X and the full stop with your ring fingers, without lifting your whole hand.

lessons.text: x. .x; six foxes. six taxis. the taxi is here. the fox is there. six.

lessons.title: Z and forward slash, the little fingers on the bottom row
lessons.tip: Z is typed by the left little finger and the forward slash by the right, at both ends of the bottom row. Let only the little finger stretch, and keep your wrist steady.

tuto.intro: Z and the forward slash are typed with the little fingers, at the ends of the bottom row. These are your weakest fingers, so give them time.

rules.d: Your left little finger goes down to Z, below A. Your right little finger goes down to the forward slash, far right, after the full stop. Do not turn your whole hand.
You see it in his/her, mum/dad, he/she. It is typed with no space on either side.
You will find it in zero, zoo, lazy, size, prize and pizza. Practise it with words and with short runs of letters.

tuto.tip: Goal: master Z and the forward slash with your little fingers, without breaking your position.

lessons.text: z/ /z z/ /z; pizza, zero, lazy, zoo; his/her; mum/dad; he/she; prize; size; puzzle

lessons.title: B and N, the inner index fingers on the bottom row
lessons.tip: B is typed by the left index finger and N by the right: your index fingers stretch towards the centre to reach them. Return to F and J straight after the keystroke.

tuto.intro: B and N complete the alphabet. Your index fingers stretch towards the centre, right at the bottom: B for the left hand, N for the right. With them, you have all 26 letters.

rules.d: Your left index finger goes down and slides right for B. Your right index finger goes down and slides left for N. Keep the movement small.
Straight after B or N, bring your index finger back to its home key. These are the keys furthest from your starting position.
With B and N, you know the whole alphabet. From here on, you can write whole sentences, even though you do not have capital letters yet.

tuto.tip: Goal: reach B and N with your index fingers without moving your other fingers, and enjoy having finished the alphabet.

lessons.text: bn nb; the new bike is blue. a brown bear is on the beach. nine big birds, ten nice bags.

lessons.title: Review: all 26 letters together
lessons.keys: z x c v b n m , . /
lessons.tip: Every letter is here. The aim of this review: no glances at the keyboard. If you hesitate over a key, pause, find it in your mind, then type.

tuto.intro: You now know the whole bottom row, so every letter of the alphabet. This review mixes all three rows.

rules.t: Do not look at the keyboard
rules.d: If you hesitate over a key, pause, find it in your mind with your finger, then type. Do not look down.
Top, middle and bottom rows become a single movement: each finger goes up, goes down and returns to its home key.
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog: this classic sentence contains all 26 letters. If you can type it without looking, you know your keyboard.

tuto.tip: Goal: move through all three rows without looking, with a smooth finger movement.

lessons.text: zxcv bnm,./ the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
